videos.description:
✅ Grab my free Cowork Toolkit - https://coworkacademy.ai/toolkit?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=v207

Most #Claude Design tutorials tell you to pick a template and start prompting, which is exactly why your slides come out generic. In this walkthrough I show you the three files to prepare first: a DESIGN.md file, a design system inside #ClaudeDesign, and a reusable presentation template, so every deck comes out polished and on-brand.

You'll grab a free DESIGN.md file from a public GitHub repo, clean it up in ChatGPT, turn it into a design system, then build a template that gets better every time you give it feedback. And even though we focus on slides, the same workflow applies to social carousels, newsletters, and any other design.

videos.title: What Emotionally Intelligent People Do Mid-Fight | Jefferson Fisher
videos.description:
You think saying how you feel will push them away. Attorney and communication expert Jefferson Fisher says the opposite, silence is what actually breaks the connection.

In this clip, Jefferson Fisher and Jay Shetty talk about what happens when you hide how you really feel in a relationship. Fisher shares why the fear of being rejected if you're honest is really the fear that you're not enough by yourself.

He walks through the number one communication mistake he sees: assuming what you said is exactly what they heard. It's not. And then he explains why most arguments aren't even about what you're arguing about, they're about the hidden need underneath: the need to feel understood, to feel heard, to feel safe.

Learn why repair isn't apologizing, and why the person who changes the narrative by 1% and does something different is the one who heals the relationship.

JAY'S DAILY WISDOM DELIVERED STRAIGHT TO YOUR INBOX
Join 900,000+ readers discovering how small daily shifts create big life change with my free newsletter. Subscribe https://news.jayshetty.me/subscribe

Chapters
0:00 — Fear of pushing people away with your truth
1:20 — The underlying fear: Am I enough by myself?
2:26 — What's said isn't what's heard
4:00 — You're fighting their identity, not their opinion
6:04 — Three ways to change someone's mind
7:36 — Opening closed doors: "I know I'm not"
8:45 — When they won't meet you halfway, be a lighthouse
10:26 — Know your goal in the conversation
12:20 — Arguments aren't to win, they're to unravel
14:02 — When your partner triggers you
15:37 — The power of breath in conflict
18:45 — Using silence as a weapon shows low EI
20:38 — If they want you, they won't make you beg
22:24 — The test: Can you sit with them in hard times?
28:31 — Repair starts with validating the unmet need
31:20 — Love is self-disclosure
